html:
Akwamu, an Akan state that dominated the coast from Accra eastward in the late 17th century, seized the Danish fort of Christiansborg at Accra in 1693 and held it for about a year.

Its leader Asameni flew his own flag over the castle and traded directly with ships, then sold it back to the Danes. Akwamu grew rich from the trade in gold and captives with the Dutch, Danes and English, and conquered the Ga towns. Its harsh rule brought revolts, and in 1730 its neighbours, led by Akyem, destroyed it. Its rise and fall came just before that of Asante. Christiansborg later became the seat of government of Ghana. See also Elmina.
sum: Akwamu, an Akan state that dominated the coast from Accra eastward in the late 17th century, seized the Danish fort of Christiansborg at Accra in 1693 and held it for about a year.
